notes: The two object markers take the 'out of' by which the English verb reaches its object (rule 16); reading 'out of' as licensed by the house nouns was the competing analysis, but those nouns keep their own English.

לְעֶזְרָה → 'it helped': the supplied subject pronoun is taken as part of the construction that recasts the prepositional predicate as a verb (rules 20 and 49). The competing reading, not previously recorded, marks 'it' added under rule 30, since it is referential rather than a dummy and realizes no morpheme; the accepted reading is kept because dropping the frame removes the preposition's own relation.
